expect.title: Critical thinking when agents do the work
headings: Actually paying attention to what's generated
"But the models will be better at this than me"
contains: Once a week, write a bit of code without an agent, or do one real thing that would suck if you forgot how to do it. (I've called this a calibration exercise, but I don't mean it as a moral one.) Once a month, write down what you've stopped doing and decide which of those you're okay not doing. One question from an old blog post of mine remains as valid as ever: How lost would you be if AI didn't exist?
I believe that the bottleneck has shifted from coding to being sure you're right.
This is what Boris Cherny calls "give Claude a way to verify its work" and I believe that this is one of the most critical components of achieving great results.
Margaret-Anne Storey has written about how this shows up in teams as an eroding understanding of a shared system theory.
comprehension debt (a term coined by Jeremy Twei)
The Claude Code team has said publicly that they rebuild understanding on demand
As I've written about before, this sort of debt is more recoverable than most engineers expect.
